content: The test image shows banana **fruits (pods)** with large dark brown/black necrotic lesions on the surface. From the part index, pod-affecting classes are **Anthracnose** and **Cigar_End_Rot**. I need to view 4 references across 4 different classes. Starting with Anthracnose pod.

Cigar_End_Rot shows dry rot at the distal tip/end of fingers — not matching the large body lesions in the test image. Need 2 more classes for the 4-class spread. Checking Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka and Cordana_Leaf_Spot.

- **Anthracnose (pod ref)**: Small discrete dark spots on green banana fruits. Test image has larger, more confluent patches — consistent with advanced/coalescing Anthracnose.
- **Cigar_End_Rot (pod ref)**: Dry rot concentrated at the distal tip of fingers — clearly does NOT match the body lesions in the test image.
- **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka / Cordana_Leaf_Spot**: Both are leaf diseases — irrelevant to the fruit-affecting symptom shown.

Only Anthracnose and Cigar_End_Rot affect pods. The test image lesions are on the fruit body (not tips), which rules out Cigar_End_Rot. Anthracnose (Colletotrichum musae) is known to produce dark sunken lesions that coalesce into large black patches on banana fruit — consistent with what's visible.
